statement: By the time a04 ran, crates/enforcer-domain/src/paths.rs (plural, not the workpack's named path.rs singular) already existed with RepoRoot and RelPath branded newtypes: private inner field, TryFrom<String>/FromStr parse-at-boundary constructors, serde try_from/into wiring, ts_rs::TS derive, Windows-drive/UNC/POSIX absolute detection for RepoRoot, and `..`-escape rejection with forward-slash normalization for RelPath. Roughly 20 consumer files across enforcer-validator, enforcer-lang-rust, enforcer-ui, enforcer-cli, enforcer-coordination, and enforcer-memory already import it as `enforcer_domain::paths::{RepoRoot, RelPath}`.
why: The workpack was authored before this reconciliation landed (likely folded in during an earlier a01/arc-02 pass) and names a file path that was never created under that name; the module is `paths` (plural) and is deeply wired into the workspace already.
howToApply: Never rename an already-wired module to match a stale workpack filename when doing so would break ~20 consumer import paths for a purely cosmetic reason. Extend the existing module in place and treat the workpack's file path as aspirational/historical, not literal, once you've confirmed via grep that consumers already depend on the real name.

statement: Added RepoRoot::resolve(&self, rel: &RelPath) -> String and RepoRoot::relativize(&self, abs: &str) -> Result<RelPath, DecodeError> to crates/enforcer-domain/src/paths.rs, the two checklist items missing from the pre-existing file. resolve joins root+rel by type (no method accepts two RelPaths or two RepoRoots as arguments, so mixing the brands is a compile error, not a runtime check). relativize strips the root prefix from an absolute string and re-validates the remainder through RelPath::try_from, reusing its existing normalization and `..`-escape rejection rather than duplicating that logic.
why: a04's Requirement Checklist explicitly named these two typed methods ("root+rel is checked and rel+rel is a type error") as the one gap between the existing paths.rs and full workpack completion; everything else (private field, parse-at-boundary, serde, normalization, fail-closed escape rejection) was already present and unchanged.
howToApply: When extending an existing branded-newtype module, prefer delegating a new fallible method's validation to the type's own TryFrom rather than re-implementing segment-walking/escape-detection inline -- keeps the escape-rejection logic in exactly one place.

statement: This worker's worktree sat on a machine running many other concurrent agent worktrees against the same physical Cargo package cache / target dir set; git checkout and cargo build/test each took 20-30 minutes due to 'Blocking waiting for file lock on package cache' / 'artifact directory' contention, not actual compile time.
why: Relevant for anyone estimating wall-clock time for a lane on this shared machine: the a04 workpack itself is small (one file, ~40 added lines + tests), but the surrounding git-reset and cargo invocations were the dominant cost.
howToApply: Budget for lock contention on shared-machine parallel lanes; prefer backgrounding long git/cargo commands and waiting on a log-file sentinel rather than polling, since foreground commands can themselves get queued behind the same lock.
